title: Measuring Hallucination in Large Language Models for Cyber Threat Intelligence: An Exploratory Study
abstract: arXiv:2611.25590v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in cyber threat intelligence (CTI) tasks, such as summarization and question answering. However, they may produce hallucinations, false or misleading content not grounded in the source text, which can mislead analysts and corrupt downstream security decisions. This paper presents an exploratory measurement study of hallucinations in LLM-based CTI. We introduce HalluVision, a reproducible framework that generates LLM outputs, extracts domain-specific entities using a fine-tuned named entity recognition model, and evaluates factual consistency using multiple similarity metrics. Using 4,940 real-world cybersecurity articles, we measure hallucinations in outputs from two commercial LLMs and one open-weight LLM. translated_title: 测量大语言模型在网络威胁情报中的幻觉现象：一项探索性研究
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）越来越多地被应用于网络威胁情报（CTI）任务，例如文本摘要和问答。然而，它们可能产生幻觉，即并非基于源文本的错误或误导性内容，这可能会误导分析师并损害下游的安全决策。本文对基于LLM的网络威胁情报任务中的幻觉现象进行了一项探索性测量研究。我们提出了HalluVision，这是一个可复现的框架，用于生成LLM输出、通过微调的命名实体识别模型提取领域特定实体，并使用多种相似度指标评估事实一致性。基于4,940篇真实世界的网络安全文章，我们测量了两个商业LLM和一个开放权重LLM输出中的幻觉现象。测量结果通过100个人工标注的输出和两个成熟的忠实度检测器进行了验证。结果显示，语义相似度与人类判断相一致，而……
tldr: 该论文提出了可复现的HalluVision框架，利用微调的命名实体识别模型和多种相似度指标，系统测量了商业及开源大语言模型在网络威胁情报任务中的幻觉现象，并发现语义相似度指标与人类判断最为一致。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces HalluVision, a reproducible framework that measures hallucinations in LLM outputs for cyber threat intelligence using fine-tuned NER and multiple similarity metrics, finding that semantic similarity aligns best with human judgments.
